title: Throttle backpressure smoothing to curb long-context spirals and tenant starvation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent 99.9th latency spikes and short-request starvation during mixed-length traffic (small prompt bursts interleaved with long-context streaming). Root cause analysis shows a feedback cascade between admission prefetch bursts, aggressive KV cache eviction, and the admission controller's slope-based credit decay leading to oscillatory backpressure ("long-context spirals"). This manifests differently per hosting mode: Hosted sees cross-tenant amplification during microbursts, Dedicated shows tenant-local throughput collapse when prefetch thrashing coincides with autoscaler scale-downs, and Private clusters experienced the issue during rolling upgrade pauses where admission state quiesced.

What we observed: telemetry showed sharp transient increases in in-flight long-sequence batches followed by a rapid admission clamp; short requests queued behind large windows and experienced 50–200x increases in p99. KV eviction_rate correlated strongly with ingress queue depth spikes. Synthetic reproduction: load-generator mix of 85% short (<=128 tokens) / 15% long (>=8192 tokens) at 1.2x normal burst reproduced the spirals on staging in ~6 minutes.

Root cause: the admission controller uses a short sliding window to estimate backlog and decays credits with a linear slope. When a sudden prefetch wave from long-context flows warms KV cache and then triggers aggressive eviction (because of host memory heuristics), subsequent small requests are denied admission for longer than intended — the admission slope overshoots due to on-host eviction latency and a lack of per-tenant shortflow reservation. Additionally, the continuous batcher combines heterogeneous lengths into mono-host kernel invocations causing head-of-line delays for short flows.

Proposed fix (multi-component):
- Admission smoothing: replace linear slope decay with an exponential moving-average (alpha=0.25) plus a minimum shortflow reservation credit so short requests get a protected fraction of admission capacity.
- Prefetch quarantine: tag prefetch-driven long-context admissions and quarantine their KV prefetch windows for a configurable grace period; prevent these prefetched frames from triggering global eviction heuristics immediately.
- KV eviction hysteresis: add a soft-hysteresis layer to host eviction that respects recent admission smoothing signals (delay aggressive quantized evictions by 2s under high-mix conditions).
- Fast-path preemption hook: allow small-batch kernels to preempt long-kernel queues at the dispatcher level, enabling immediate servicing of latency-sensitive requests.
- Feature flags and rollout knobs: server-side flag admission.smoothing.enabled, per-tenant shortflow_pct, and prefetch.quarantine_ms.

Trade-offs: these changes slightly reduce maximum batch packing efficiency for certain long-only workloads (expected throughput drop ~3–6%) but dramatically improves 99.9 latency for short requests and reduces customer escalations. KV hysteresis increases short-term memory pressure and may increase soft OOM risk if not tuned; mitigation is conservative defaults and observability.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged canary on internal staging with the synthetic mixed-load harness (target: 100% reproduction mitigation).
2) Canary in Hosted on 5% of traffic (non-critical regions) for 48h. Monitor short p50/p99, queue_depth, kv_eviction_rate, admission_rejects, and customer error spikes.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% for Hosted if no regression; run Dedicated canary on a reserved pool with heavy mixed workloads before org-wide Dedicated rollout.
4) For Private customers, offer an opt-in patch and runbook; coordinate with SRE and customer on upgrade window.

Observability & SLOs to watch: ingress.short_p99_ms, ingress.long_p99_ms, queue_depth_95, kv_evictions_per_min, admission_reject_rate, tenant_shortflow_latency_ratio, customer_escalation_count. Alert thresholds and runbook included in linked Confluence.

Rollback/hotfix plan: server flag off reverts all runtime behavior. If KV hysteresis causes memory pressure, hotpatch knob prefetch.quarantine_ms=0 and revert eviction changes via runtime feature config. Emergency measure: enable 'transparent-admission-expiry' (pre-existing kill-switch) to collapse admission windows and restore baseline behavior.

2026-03-11 - Investigation: telemetry owner (infra-observability) confirmed kv_eviction_rate spike aligns with admission clamps. Created synthetic workload that reliably reproduces within 6 minutes.

2026-03-12 - Prototype: Marcus implemented admission smoothing prototype (ema-based) and shortflow token bucket. Local perf bench shows 4% throughput loss under long-only load but p99 short latency reduced by 85%.

2026-03-13 - Code review: PR opened (link in links). Design review notes: ensure feature flags exposed to Dedicated control plane; add opt-in for Private customers. Security sign-off not required per initial review.

2026-03-14 - QA: ran canary harness on staging. Two flaky test failures unrelated (kernel scheduler timer drift) — added a guard. PM (Rohit Srinivasan) approved canary rollout for low-traffic Hosted region; coordinating Dedicated pool window next week.

Follow-ups: add a low-overhead host gauge for admission_smoothed_value, and coordinate with Billing to observe cost delta for heavy long-only tenants. Postmortem to be included in incident doc after production verification.
